findings.assessment: The gap is real and the blind's diagnosis of WHY is exact. x-opensip-payload-registry closes WHICH documents a parameter may cite and refuses two REGISTRY ROWS resolving to one document digest (PAYLOAD_PARAMETER_AMBIGUOUS_ROW). Nothing anywhere constrained how many SPEC ENTRIES may cite one row. The two questions are one level apart and the registry's own prose reasons carefully about the first while never reaching the second. Consequence: identity closure admitted both entries, workflows.verify_scope_parameter_binding is EXISTENTIAL over the selected rows and returned a verified digest for whichever document the caller happened to hold, and both entries entered analysisSpecDigest and therefore PlanId - so two conforming hosts could bind different scope policies from ONE admitted Plan and attribute the E2->E3 comparison scope axis differently for the same PlanId.
findings.whyRootsPreferredSemanticsIsSound: At most one is the only answer that does not invent authority. A default, a first-listed or last-listed winner, or a merge would each be the registry making the arbitrary selection its own law declines to make one level up - and the digest recipes give no basis for preferring either payload. Zero must stay legal because most analyses need no scope-policy input, and the caller that DOES need it already meets an explicit missing-selection refusal, so nothing is silently substituted. Critically, the foundation scope-descriptor named by plan.scopeDigest is a different record under no parameter row at all, and it must not become a fallback; that is asserted rather than assumed.
findings.generalisationProposed: The law is published for the parameter CLASS, not for the ScopeDocumentV1 row alone. Both registered rows are Plan INPUTS and the ambiguity argument is identical for either, so a rule written for one row would have left the sibling case to be rediscovered - exactly the failure mode being corrected. ImportSourceContextV1's existing zero/one/multiple rule is unchanged and is now TOTAL rather than reachable only from the import derivation.

precedenceNamed.atRetainedClosure: MOST SPECIFIC FIRST. The retained analysis-spec is schema-validated by payload(...,'analysis-spec') before anything else, so a WHOLE-ITEM duplicate refuses on uniqueItems first and never reports the selection key (measured: the observed text is jsonschema's 'uniqueItems'). IMPORT_SOURCE_CONTEXT_MULTIPLE keeps its name inside the import derivation that consumes that row. admit_parameter_selection runs after that block as the total backstop, and names the offending row: ANALYSIS_SPEC_PARAMETER_SELECTION_AMBIGUOUS:<row key>.
precedenceNamed.atThePrePlanBoundary: cardinality -> schema -> native vocabulary -> foundation selection law. Step 4 is APPENDED so the three published steps keep their exact order and no existing route is reclassified; steps 1-3 never read `parameters`, so only the first-reported fault of a doubly-bad spec is decided by this placement.
precedenceNamed.atTheWorkflowVerifier: zero rows -> the existing BASELINE.SCOPE_NOT_A_SELECTED_PARAMETER; more than one -> the new ambiguity refusal, BEFORE any payload comparison; exactly one and mismatched -> the existing BASELINE.SCOPE_PARAMETER_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Order matters: checking the digest first would let a caller holding one of two candidates obtain a 'verified' digest, which is the existential proof that made the two entries indistinguishable.

findings.errorVocabulary: No new public vocabulary. Uniqueness of the ownership tuple is a DETERMINACY property of what the record MEANS and must hold wherever the record is read. findings.assessment: Real. Section 4.1 commits the examined-partition question in two places and no rule joined them. RC-2 reads examinedExhaustive only for a RESOLVED rung, so on the twelve non-resolved pairs nothing read it at all - and file@enumerated is one of them, which is why the vector chose it. That entry is not a harmless inconsistency there: coverage=complete on file@enumerated carries the inventory-totality obligation, which keys on `coverage` alone. RC-1's published sentence 'examinedExhaustive stays the independent examined-partition claim of section 4.1' is an accurate half-truth - independent of the RESOLUTION STATE - and reading it as unconstrained is what left the join unstated. That sentence is corrected to say what it meant.
findings.whereIDisagreeWithTheBlind: Its title calls coverage and examinedExhaustive 'TWO committed encodings of ONE claim' and proposes 'an equality the closure decides'. An EQUALITY would be wrong and would refuse lawful evidence. examinedExhaustive is about the EXAMINATION; coverage is the ANSWER over what was examined. A host may examine the committed partition exhaustively and still answer `unknown` because the evidence it needs is MISSING rather than unexamined - ambiguous or missing Rust compilation ownership, an undeclared or unservable capability, an unlisted source variant. An equality would force a host to understate its own examination in order to report an honest unknown, and would refuse exactly the disclosures section 10 requires. So the published rule is one-directional: coverage=complete REQUIRES examinedExhaustive=true; coverage=unknown constrains it in NEITHER direction. Both unknown positives are asserted by controls and by reference cases so a later reader cannot quietly tighten it.
findings.totality: RC-6 runs before the rung branch and without a `continue`, so it is total over every registered (relation, rung) pair - all 17, asserted by a loop - resolved or not, and independent of the RC-1/RC-2 state rules, which still report on the same entry. It needs no fact: asserted equal for an empty fact set and a non-matching one, which is the fact-free shape a fact-admission guard cannot protect. RC-0 still runs first, so an unregistered pair keeps its own name.
findings.readsTheFieldOnlyWhenCarried: `coverage` is a required member of ViewEntryV3 and the producer boundary schema-validates before calling the helper, so every real entry carries it. The three pre-existing DIRECT coverage_bijection cases pass a bare resolutionCompleteness fragment with no `coverage` at all; inventing a claim for them would be the checker asserting something the caller never made, so the rule reads the field only when present. That is stated in the code rather than left to be inferred.
